S7 Class for the Quadratic Penalty

Source: R/quadratic_penalty.R
QuadraticPenalty.Rd

QuadraticPenalty is the class of the objects that quadratic_penalty() builds. Beyond the seven properties that every penalty carries, it stores the matrix \(P\), the rank of \(D'PD\), an orthonormal basis of the null space of \(D'PD\), the log pseudo-determinant of \(D'PD\) and the assembled \(D'PD\). All five are computed once at construction and are independent of the hyperparameter, so every quantity of the branch is closed form in \(\lambda\).

Usage

QuadraticPenalty(
  penalty_name = character(0),
  map = NULL,
  n_coef = integer(0),
  params = character(0),
  params_bounds = list(),
  link_params = list(),
  params_smooth = logical(0),
  P = NULL,
  p_rank = integer(0),
  null_basis = NULL,
  logpdet_DPD = integer(0),
  DPD = NULL,
  tol = 1e-10
)

Arguments

penalty_name

A single string naming the penalty, used by print() and by any code that reports which penalty a block carries.

map

The matrix \(D\), of \(m\) rows and \(q\) columns, or NULL for the identity. A Matrix object is kept in its own storage, so a diagonal map, such as the map that standardization produces, is recognized as diagonal by its class.

n_coef

The number of coefficients \(q\). The value is a single whole number.

params

The hyperparameter names, in the order by which every derivative list is keyed. The value is character(0) for a penalty with none.

params_bounds

A named list with one entry per hyperparameter, and each entry is a numeric pair giving an open interval. A value at either endpoint is rejected, so (0, Inf) excludes zero.

link_params

A named list, one linkfunctions7 link per hyperparameter, carrying that hyperparameter's own interval onto the whole real line.

params_smooth

A logical vector, one entry per hyperparameter, TRUE where the value is differentiable in it.

P

The symmetric positive semidefinite matrix of the quadratic form, with as many rows as the map has, or as many as there are coefficients when the map is NULL. It is a dgCMatrix under blocks > 1.

p_rank

The rank of \(D'PD\), a single whole number, counted at construction by a relative eigenvalue rule. Without a map it is the rank of \(P\).

null_basis

An orthonormal basis of the null space of \(D'PD\), with n_coef rows and n_coef - p_rank columns, and no columns when the penalty is full rank.

logpdet_DPD

The log pseudo-determinant of \(D'PD\): the sum of the logarithms of its non-zero eigenvalues. It is a single number. Without a map it is the log pseudo-determinant of \(P\).

DPD

The assembled \(D'PD\), an n_coef by n_coef matrix, cached so that the gradient and the Hessian never re-form it.

tol

The relative eigenvalue tolerance, a single positive number, 1e-10 by default. quadratic_penalty() counts p_rank at this tolerance and stores it, and check_penalty() counts the eigenvalues of the matrix at the same tolerance when it compares them with the rank.

Value

An S7 object of class QuadraticPenalty, inheriting from penalty(), with the seven inherited properties and the six above.

Details

Construct through quadratic_penalty(), which computes the five properties and checks that \(P\) is symmetric and positive semidefinite. This raw constructor takes them as given and does not check any of them. A wrong rank passed here enters the value, the hyperparameter derivatives, penalty_rank(), penalty_logpdet() and is_proper(), and check_penalty() does not detect it, because every one of its rows reads the same stored rank.

Methods

This section lists the methods registered on this class, by the page that documents each.

  • The value and its coefficient derivatives: penalty_value(), penalty_gradient() and penalty_hessian().

  • The hyperparameter derivatives: penalty_grad_theta(), penalty_hess_theta() and penalty_cross().

  • The predicates: penalty_kinks(), is_proper() and is_quadratic().

  • The quantities of a marginal criterion: penalty_matrix(), penalty_rank(), penalty_null_basis() and penalty_logpdet().

  • The higher derivatives of a marginal criterion: penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian(), penalty_dcross() and beta_quadratic().

  • The movement of the Hessian with the coefficients: penalty_dhessian_beta(), penalty_d2hessian_beta() and penalty_dhessian_beta_theta(). The last two return zero matrices because the Hessian does not depend on the coefficients, and are documented on the page of the base-class methods.

  • The proximal operator: penalty_prox().

The class has no penalty_prox_spec(), penalty_draw() or penalty_readable() method of its own, so those generics dispatch to the methods of the base class penalty().

See also

quadratic_penalty() for the constructor to use, penalty_value.QuadraticPenalty() for what the branch computes, structured_penalty() and additive_penalty() for the other branches for which is_quadratic() returns TRUE.

Examples

pen <- quadratic_penalty(crossprod(diff(diag(5), differences = 2)))
S7::S7_inherits(pen, QuadraticPenalty)
#> [1] TRUE

# These are three of the six properties, all computed at construction.
pen@p_rank
#> [1] 3
dim(pen@null_basis)
#> [1] 5 2
pen@logpdet_DPD
#> [1] 3.912023
